mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined for three straight weeks (3.9 to 2.4), so fewer people are staying home; every point of decline releases household trips into the community and lifts retail and recreation footfall over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 3.9 to 2.4 across the four weekly means
failure_condition: The next-28-day RETAIL_REC mean is at or below the last-28-day mean of -14.75 while RESIDENTIAL continues its three-week decline.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT breaks its four-week plateau when the latest week improves more than 2 points (-21.4 to -17.6); restored transit capacity enables discretionary trips and pulls RETAIL_REC above its trailing level within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean improves by more than 2.0 points versus the prior week.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -21.4 to -17.6 in the latest week
failure_condition: After a TRANSIT week-on-week gain above 2 points, RETAIL_REC fails to exceed -10.3 at any point over the following 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS jumping to 44.3 above baseline marks a warm-weather outdoor-leisure onset; park outings are bundled with errands, so a park surge above +40 leads RETAIL_REC gains by roughly two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean exceeds +40.0 percent above baseline.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from 17.3 to 44.3 in the latest week
failure_condition: In the two weeks after PARKS exceeds +40, RETAIL_REC weekly means remain at or below the trailing 28-day mean of -14.75.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES falls (-8.3 to -11.6) while TRANSIT improves (-21.4 to -17.6) in the same week, showing trips shifting from commuting to leisure destinations; retail and recreation trips substitute for work trips and RETAIL_REC rises over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES weekly mean falls while TRANSIT weekly mean rises in the same week.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell 3.3 points while TRANSIT rose 3.8 points in the latest week
failure_condition: In weeks where WORKPLACES falls and TRANSIT rises together, the next-28-day RETAIL_REC mean does not exceed the last-28-day mean of -14.75.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM (16.1) and PARKS (44.3) both set four-week highs in the same week, indicating broad household out-of-home re-engagement; paired errand-plus-leisure trips raise RETAIL_REC within one week because retail sits adjacent to those destinations.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS both set a four-week high in the same week.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM 16.1 and PARKS 44.3 are both four-week maxima at t-0w
failure_condition: The week after a joint GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS four-week high shows RETAIL_REC no higher than the t-1w value of -15.6.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC momentum: the latest weekly mean rose 5.3 points to -10.3 against a trailing 28-day mean of -14.75; if the current level merely persists, the arithmetic mean over the next 28 days exceeds the prior 28-day mean.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC weekly mean rises more than 3.0 points versus the prior week.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose from -15.6 to -10.3 in the latest week against a 28-day mean of -14.75
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC falls back below -14.75 within two weeks, dragging the next-28-day mean below the last-28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Under an easing-restrictions regime, successive transit gains lower the perceived cost of moving around and retail converges back toward baseline; RETAIL_REC rises over four weeks as long as TRANSIT keeps improving and RESIDENTIAL keeps drifting down.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves for two consecutive weeks while RESIDENTIAL keeps falling.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved 3.8 points while RESIDENTIAL fell 0.7 points in the latest week
failure_condition: In an easing regime with two consecutive TRANSIT gains and falling RESIDENTIAL, the next-28-day RETAIL_REC mean stays at or below -14.75.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES deepening from -8.3 to -11.6 signals a renewed shift to remote work that strips weekday commuter and lunchtime foot traffic; RETAIL_REC declines over the next two weeks relative to the last four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES weekly mean falls by more than 2.5 points versus the prior week.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES dropped from -8.3 to -11.6 in the latest week
failure_condition: After a WORKPLACES drop greater than 2.5 points, RETAIL_REC weekly means stay above -10.3 for two consecutive weeks.
